newsitem.title: USA: 3M says on track to post record '97 results.
newsitem.headline: 3M says on track to post record '97 results.

text.p: Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co (3M) said Wednesday it is on target to post record 1997 results despite the effects of the strong U.S. dollar.
3M's second quarter sales rose 8.4 percent to $3.8 billion, but changes in currency exchange rates cut overall sales by nearly four percent.
Sales volume was up 13 percent overall, and selling prices were down slightly.

3M reported second quarter earnings of $1.01 percent, but the strength of the U.S. dollar cut profits by an estimated $0.05 a share. Costs were also higher to invest in the company's "Pacing Plus" new products programs, 3M said.
According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estiamtes was $1.03 a share.
"Looking ahead, we expect our solid performance to continue in the second half of this year," L.D. DeSimone, 3M chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.

"While the stronger U.S. dollar will continue to impact us, we are on track to deliver record 1997 results as we continue to implement our growth initiatives in the United States and abroad," he added.
In the United States, second quarter sales rose about 10 percent to $1.8 billion, driven by volume gains.

Internationally, sales topped $2 billion for the first time despite a seven percent negative currency effect, the company said. Volume abroad increased 15 percent and selling prices were down about one percent.
